sentences.text: The stout humerus suggests that Xenerodiops had a robust physical structure.
The mobile rostrum suggests that Xenerodiops was capable of delivering a powerful bite.
The genus name Xenerodiops is derived from Greek words meaning 'stranger heron resemblance'.
The species name mycter comes from the Greek word for 'nose'.
Fossil remains of Xenerodiops were discovered in Egypt by Elwyn L. Simons and formally described in 1987.
Xenerodiops is classified in its own family, Xenerodiopidae, though some researchers argue this family is synonymous with the heron family Ardeidae.
When described, herons were classified in the order Ciconiiformes, which has since been split and now places herons in Pelecaniformes.
Some researchers have synonymized the family Xenerodiopidae with Ardeidae because the beak shape resembles that of the Nycticoracinae subfamily.
Xenerodiops lived during the Oligocene epoch, approximately 33 million years ago.
The time range for Xenerodiops is estimated to be between 33.9 and 27.3 million years ago.
Fossils of Xenerodiops have been found in Egypt, though it may also be present in Libya.
It is debated whether Xenerodiops mycter and Zeltornis ginsburgi are the same species, as they were described from different fossil parts.
